Pixel XL is selected by default

Pixel XL enables Unlimited Original Quality Google Photos backup at no storage cost. If you prefer newer editing features (e.g. Magic Eraser, Ultra HDR), you can switch to a newer Pixel in the settings anytime.
Even though Pixel XL is already selected, Google Photos will not apply the spoofing until it is completely stopped and reopened. Tap the button below to apply changes immediately.
Force-stop scoped apps after changing settings to apply
Photos and videos backed up from Pixel XL do not count toward your Google Account storage quota at Original Quality or Storage Saver quality.
Free backup applies ONLY when Google Photos backup quality is set to "Storage saver". Original Quality will consume your Google Account storage quota!

Pixel 6 and newer devices do NOT include free unlimited cloud backup. All uploads consume Google Account storage quota. If you want unlimited album storage, select Pixel XL (Original quality) or Pixel 2–5 (Storage saver).

Two Ways to Verify Unlimited Backup:

1. Check Google Photos Backup Settings
- Open Google Photos.
- Tap your profile icon at top-right > Backup.
- Tap the gear icon at top-right.
- Check that the banner displays: “This Pixel can back up unlimited photos & videos at no charge.”

2. Upload a Photo & Check Storage Details
- Back up a new photo or video in Google Photos.
- Open the photo and swipe up to view details (or view info on photos.google.com).
- Check that the storage section states: “This item doesn’t take up space in your account storage” (0 bytes used).

Troubleshooting & Diagnostics:
- Check Diagnostics: Open Diagnostics to inspect individual hook registrations and the separate Build-field VERIFY readback; neither proves Google Photos intercepted the relevant API.
- Check Backup Quality: Pixel 2–5 require Storage saver quality for free unlimited quota. Original quality will consume Google Account storage.
- Clear App Cache: If Google Photos cached old device properties, tap Force-stop scoped apps or clear Google Photos app cache and restart.
Profile unavailable; settings could not be read.

1. Google Photos > Avatar > Backup > Backup settings (gear icon): check for the unlimited backup banner.
2. Upload a photo > swipe up on photo: confirm “This item doesn’t take up space in your account storage” (0 bytes used).

If quota is consumed, an OK result below confirms only Build-field readback; it does not prove Google Photos features/hooks worked. Ensure backup quality matches model conditions (e.g. Storage saver for Pixel 2–5), and force-stop Google Photos to clear stale cache.
Build fields: real vs spoof target

Values are read in this module-app process (the real device), not inside Google Photos. The separate VERIFY result is a readback of Build fields in the hooked process; neither result proves a target API was intercepted.

The service connection only reports whether this app is connected to the Xposed manager; it does not mean hooks are active. Package-ready is a lifecycle callback, not hook success. Check each method\'s registration result below; even all registered means only that the framework accepted registration, not that Google Photos called the method or received a spoofed value. Runtime observation confirms an interceptor was entered at least once. VERIFY separately reads back Build fields in the hooked process. Use "Copy diagnostics report" when reporting an issue — it includes scope and device Build values, but no account data.
Legacy VERIFY detail (both SystemProperties overloads registered): %1$s
Build readback OK (not proof Photos hooks/features work)
No VERIFY record yet for this verified current-boot run. Open Google Photos once, wait a few seconds, then reopen this screen.
No VERIFY record yet for this verified current run. The package-ready callback has not been observed; this does not establish whether it ran.
unknown (legacy or unverified-origin VERIFY; no OS-verified run identity)
unknown (prior-boot VERIFY from an OS-verified origin; historical, not current)
unknown (OS-verified origin, but current boot could not be confirmed)
Historical prior-boot run (OS-verified origin): no VERIFY record was recorded for that run; this says nothing about the current run.
OS-verified run, but its boot epoch is unavailable or cannot be matched: no VERIFY record can be classified as current.
No VERIFY record can be linked to an OS-verified run; current-run status is unknown.
No VERIFY record or OS-verified run identity is available; current-run status is unknown.
Diagnostics data could not be read; its state is unavailable (not an empty telemetry result).

Hook telemetry is unavailable because the diagnostics token is not synchronized to Xposed remote preferences. The hooked process cannot deliver telemetry, so this is not an empty result. Restart LSPosed (or toggle the module) so the manager service rebinds, then reopen Google Photos and this screen.
Hook telemetry is unavailable (diagnostics token not synchronized).
OS-verified origin; current boot could not be confirmed.

Xposed manager service is not connected. This only describes this app\'s manager connection and does not establish whether hooks ran in Google Photos. Enable this module in LSPosed, open Google Photos, then reopen this screen.
Refreshing diagnostics because the service state changed. Captured values are temporarily unavailable.
Connected to the Xposed manager; preferences and the diagnostics token are syncing. Diagnostics may be temporarily unavailable. This does not indicate whether hooks ran.
Connected to the Xposed manager, but settings synchronization failed. Remote writes remain disabled; check the manager connection and retry.
The Xposed manager connection was lost. Settings are read-only until the service reconnects and preferences are ready.
Settings cannot be saved until the Xposed service is ready again. Your changes were not saved.
Saved for this process, but disk persistence is uncertain. Keep the app open until the Xposed service syncs your changes.
The service changed while diagnostics were being read. Nothing was copied; please retry.
No lifecycle milestones have been recorded yet. Hook registration results, if available, are shown separately. Open Google Photos once, wait a few seconds, then reopen this screen.
No lifecycle milestones were recorded for this prior-boot run. Hook registration results, if available, are shown separately.
Historical/prior-boot records from an OS-verified origin; not current evidence.
OS-verified origin; the run boot could not be matched to the current boot. Lifecycle and hook data below have unverified currentness and are not current evidence.
No lifecycle milestones were recorded for an OS-verified run whose current boot could not be established. This is unknown historical data, not evidence about the current run.
Module loaded in a scoped process (%1$s).

No package-load callback was recorded for this run. Check the configured scope and reopen the target app; absence of a record alone does not establish whether a callback occurred or why it is missing.
No package-load callback was recorded for that prior-boot run. Missing data alone does not establish whether a callback occurred or why it is missing.
No package-load callback was recorded for an OS-verified run whose currentness is unknown. Missing data does not describe the current run or establish why the record is missing.
Package loaded; package-ready callback not observed yet. This is not evidence that the package never became ready or that the framework/API is incompatible.
Package was loaded; a package-ready callback was not recorded for that prior-boot run. This does not establish whether the callback occurred or why it is missing.
Package was loaded in a run whose currentness is unknown; no package-ready record can be treated as current or as "not observed yet".
Last package-ready callback observed: %1$s (%2$s). This is lifecycle evidence only; see registration results below.
Last Build-field VERIFY readback passed (nativeReady=%1$s); this does not verify feature hooks or Photos behavior.
Last Build-field VERIFY readback failed: %1$s (nativeReady=%2$s). See the copied diagnostics report or enable verbose logging.
VERIFY ran but no result was recorded (unexpected).
Legacy or unverified-origin VERIFY data has no OS-verified run identity; its outcome is unknown.
Prior-boot VERIFY from an OS-verified origin is historical; its result is unknown, not current.
VERIFY has an OS-verified origin, but the run boot could not be matched to the current boot; result is unknown.
VERIFY has a future timestamp (%1$s); clock anomaly, stale and not treated as a current result.
Package-ready ran but no VERIFY result was recorded; enable verbose logging in Advanced options and retry.
Package-ready was observed, but no VERIFY result was recorded for that prior-boot run. This is historical and does not describe the current run.
Package-ready was recorded for a run whose currentness is unknown, but no VERIFY result is recorded; current-run VERIFY state is unknown.
not observed (may not have been called; absence is not proof)
All registrations do not prove Google Photos called a target API. An observed entry only proves an interceptor was entered, not that it ran for Google Photos or returned a spoofed value.
